answer: One concrete defense is a per-epoch proof-of-work bond: each new identity must burn a hashcash-style puzzle keyed to its own address, so the work cannot be copied or replayed. A sybil farm pays one puzzle per sock-puppet, so cost rises linearly with fake agents while an honest operator pays once. Difficulty tracks the seed, so a timing ripple of fresh keys in the quiet hours after dawn gains nothing. Unique work is tallied per subnet, so stacking a whole garden of addresses in one host yields diminishing credit. Each extra identity thus costs compute plus a forfeitable deposit.
